'''Pekka Tarjanne''' (1937–2010) was a scientist and politician who served as the chairman of the [[Liberals (Finland)|Liberal Party]] and minister of transport in Finland. He also headed the [[International Telecommunication Union]] from 1989 and 1999.

==Early life and education==
Tarjanne was born in [[Stockholm]], Sweden, on 19 September 1937.<ref name=ptrem/><ref name=edus/> His grandfather was one of the founders of the Liberal Party and served as the minister of interior.<ref name=timd/>

In 1960 Tarjanne obtained his master of science degree in engineering and a PhD degree in technology from [[Helsinki University of Technology]] at age 24.<ref name=edus>{{cite web|title=Pekka Tarjanne|url=https://www.eduskunta.fi/FI/kansanedustajat/Sivut/910170.aspx|publisher=Finnish Parliament|access-date=10 August 2022}}</ref><ref name=posti/>

==Career==
Tarjanne carried out research and teaching in Denmark and the United States and returned to Finland in 1965.<ref name=itubio/> He was promoted to the professorship in [[theoretical physics]] at the [[University of Oulu]].<ref name=itubio/> From 1967 he worked as a professor in the same field at the [[University of Helsinki]].<ref name=posti/> He served as the chairman of the Liberal Party from 1968 to 1978.<ref name=itubio/> He became one of the youngest party leaders on record when he was elected to the post.<ref name="timd">{{cite news|title=Nuclear leader|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/CS134968155/TTDA?u=wikipedia&sid=bookmark-TTDA&xid=112c370e|access-date=4 October 2023|work=The Times Diary|issue=58007|date=27 October 1970}}</ref>

On 23 March 1970 Tarjanne was elected to the Finnish Parliament where he served until 20 September 1977.<ref name=edus/><ref name=itubio/> He was the minister of transport and communications and the state minister responsible for Nordic cooperation between 4 September 1972 and 12 June 1975 in the [[Sorsa I Cabinet|cabinet]] led by [[Prime Minister of Finland|Prime Minister]] [[Kalevi Sorsa]].<ref name=edus/><ref name=posti/> In 1977 Tarjanne was appointed director-general of posts and telecommunications which he held until 1989.<ref name=posti>{{cite web|title=Pekka Tarjanne
|url=https://www.postimuseo.fi/postin-paajohtajat/en/10.html|publisher=Postimuseo|access-date=10 August 2022}}</ref> In 1989 he was elected secretary-general of the International Telecommunication Union in the conference held in [[Nice]], France.<ref name=itubio/> He replaced [[Richard E. Butler]] in the post.<ref>{{cite magazine|author=Ray Le Maistre|title=Child of the '70s|access-date=4 October 2023|issue=9|magazine=Communications International|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/213153629|date=September 1999|location=London|volume=26
|id={{ProQuest|213153629}}}}</ref> Tarjanne was re-elected to the same post in the conference in [[Kyoto]], Japan, in 1994<ref name=itubio>{{cite web|title=Past and Present Senior Officials|access-date=10 August 2022|url=https://www.itu.int/en/history/Pages/ElectedOfficialBio.aspx?off=38
|publisher=International Telecommunication Union}}</ref> and held the post until 1999.<ref name=ptrem/> His successor as the secretary-general of the International Telecommunication Union was [[Yoshio Utsumi]].<ref>{{cite magazine|title=ITU Chief Gets Acquainted|date=7 June 1999|volume=3
|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/275112283|access-date=4 October 2023|magazine=Wireless Today|issue=108
|id={{ProQuest|275112283}}}}</ref>

He was the deputy CEO of a Bermuda-based company, Project Oxygen Ltd between 1999 and 2000.<ref name=edus/> Tarjanne also served as the special advisor to the [[Secretary-General of the United Nations]] on information and communication technologies at the beginning of the 2000s.<ref>{{cite web|title=World Chronicle 851: Pekka Tarjanne, Information and Communication Technologies|publisher=UN|access-date=11 August 2022|date=14 December 2001|url=https://www.unmultimedia.org/avlibrary/asset/2170/2170523/}}</ref> As of 2003 and 2004 he was professor at the Academy of Technology and the chair of the eight-member International Award Selection Committee.<ref>{{cite news|title=Finland launches the largest technology prize in the world|url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/588745|access-date=10 August 2022|work=EurekAlert}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Web inventor wins top technology prize|url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2004/apr/15/elearning.research|access-date=10 August 2022|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=15 April 2004}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==
Tarjanne was married.<ref name=ptrem/> He died in [[Hattula]] on 24 February 2010.<ref name=ptrem>{{cite web|title=Pekka Tarjanne remembered
|url=https://www.itu.int/net/itunews/issues/2010/03/04.aspx|publisher=International Telecommunication Union|access-date=10 August 2022}}</ref><ref name=edus/>

===Recognition===
Tarjanne and his wife, Aino, were named by Geneva State Council as the honorary citizens for their "major contribution to enhancing Geneva's reputation as an international centre".<ref name=ptrem/>
